record.original_question: Is the variety of ℓ-groups generated by all nilpotent ℓ-groups finitely based?

evidence.quote: 1.52. (V. V. Bludov, A. M. W. Glass [17]) Is the variety of ℓ-groups generated by all nilpotent ℓ-groups finitely based?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) is an algebraic structure (G, ·, ⁻¹, e, ∨, ∧) such that (G, ·, ⁻¹, e) is a group, (G, ∨, ∧) is a lattice, and the group multiplication distributes over the lattice operations on both sides (i.e., a(b∨c)d = abd ∨ acd and a(b∧c)d = abd ∧ acd for all a,b,c,d ∈ G). An ℓ-group is called nilpotent if its underlying group is nilpotent. A variety of ℓ-groups is a class of ℓ-groups closed under taking ℓ-subgroups, ℓ-homomorphic images, and direct products; equivalently, by Birkhoff's theorem, it is the class of all ℓ-groups satisfying some set of equations in the language (·, ⁻¹, e, ∨, ∧). A variety is said to be finitely based if it can be axiomatized by finitely many such equations.

Let 𝒩 denote the variety of ℓ-groups generated by the class of all nilpotent ℓ-groups. Determine whether 𝒩 is finitely based.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Bludov and Glass, appears to remain open. Recent literature on the variety generated by all nilpotent lattice-ordered groups continues to investigate related conjectures (e.g., Kopytov's question about weakly Abelian ℓ-groups) and rules out candidate counterexamples, but no finite equational basis has been established or refuted.
